questions.question: Which of the following is the tenure of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Comptroller and Auditor General of India__

 __
 
• Article 148 provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG).
 
• The Comptroller and Auditor General is appointed by the President of India and can be removed from office only in the manner and on the grounds that a Judge of the Supreme Court is removed.
 
• He is appointed for a period of 6 years or until attaining the age of 65 years whichever is earlier.
 
• He is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.
 
• He acts as a guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system of the country at both the Centre and the state levels.
 
• He primarily works to uphold the Constitution of India and the laws of Parliament in the terms of financial administration.
 
• Current Comptroller and Auditor-General of India: Girish Chandra Murmu​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• V. Narahari Rao__

 
 
• He was an Indian civil servant who served the Indian Audit and Accounts Service in post-independence India.
 
• He served as the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India from 1948 to 1954.
 
• The Government of India awarded him the third highest civilian honor of the Padma Bhushan in 1954 for his contributions to civil service.

questions.question: The concept of microfinance is primarily aimed at providing financial services to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low-income individuals and small businesses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Microfinance is a way in which loans, credit, insurance, access to savings accounts, and money transfers are provided to small business owners and entrepreneurs in underdeveloped parts of India.
 
• Microfinance is a form of financial service that provides small loans and other financial services to poor and low-income households, hence it is an economic tool designed to promote financial inclusion which enables the poor and low-income households to come out of poverty, increase their income levels, and improve overall living standards.
 
• The beneficiaries of microfinance are those who do not have access to traditional financial resources.
 
• Interest rates on microloans are generally higher than those on a traditional personal loan as the amount of the loan is small. 
 
• Features of microfinance:
 
 
• The borrowers are generally from low-income backgrounds. 
 
• Loans availed under microfinance are usually of small amounts, i.e., microloans. 
 
• The loan tenure is short.
 
• Microfinance loans do not require any collateral. 
 
• These loans are usually repaid at higher frequencies.
 
• The purpose of most microfinance loans is income generation.
 
• The end result of microloans should be to have its recipients outgrow smaller loans and be ready for traditional bank loans.

questions.question: _____ is a legendary sitar player and one of India's most esteemed classical musicians.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Ravi Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Pandit Ravi Shankar**

 
 
• Pandit Ravi Shankar was a virtuoso sitar player and a composer who played a pivotal role in popularizing Indian classical music around the world.
 
• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in recognition of his exceptional contribution to music.
 
• Ravi Shankar collaborated with several international musicians, notably George Harrison of The Beatles, which helped introduce sitar to western audiences in the 1960s.
 
• He was influential in the development of the fusion music genre, combining elements of Eastern and Western music to create unique sounds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Ustad Zakir Hussain​**

 
 
• Ustad Zakir Hussain is associated with the musical instrument, Tabla.
 
• He collaborated with the famous American band 'The Beatles' which deserves special mention.
 
• He was designated with awards:
 
 
• ​Padma Shri in 1988
 
• Padma Bhushan in 2002
 
• Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1990
 
• United States National Endowment for the Arts National Heritage Fellowship, the highest award given to traditional artists and musicians by the USA.
 
 
 
 
 
• ** Ustad Bismillah Khan**
 
 
• Ustad Bismillah Khan used to play Shehnai.
 
• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916 – 2006) (Real name is Qamaruddin Khan), was an Indian musician credited with popularizing the Shehnai.
 
• Shehnai is a musical instrument that is similar to the oboe (common in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.)
 
• He was felicitated with several awards including:
 
 
• Padma Shri in 1961
 
• Padma Bhushan in 1968
 
• Padma Vibhushan in 1980
 
• Bharat Ratna in 2001
 
 
 
• He also played the Shehnai at the 1st Republic Day celebration in 1950.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Bhimsen Joshi **
 
 
• Born on** 4 February 1922 in Gadak district of Karnataka.**
 
• He was fond of music since childhood.
 
• He was greatly influenced by Abdul Karim Khan, the founder of Kirana Gharana.
 
• In 1933 he left home in search of Guru. He stayed in Bijapur, Pune and Gwalior for the next two years.
 
• He also took music lessons from **Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan of Gwalior.**
 
• He received his early education in classical music from Pandit Rambhau Kundgolkar, a disciple of Abdul Karim Khan.
 
• He visited Calcutta and Punjab before returning home.
 
• By 1937, Pandit Bhimsen Joshi had become a well-known khyal singer. There he also learned the nuances of khayal singing from Sawai Gandharva for many years.
 
• Besides singing, he has also mastered thumri and bhajan.
 
• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi passed away on 25 January 2011.
 
• On 4 November 2008, he was selected for the country's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna Award, India's highest civilian honor, which was awarded in 1975 with the Padma Bhushan in the arts.
 
• Pt. Bhimsen Joshi has been awarded many honors and distinctions including Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

questions.question: On July 27, 2023, Prime Minister Narendra Modi released ____ installment of PM-KISAN of about Rs. 17,000 crores to more than 8.5 crore beneficiaries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) scheme provides financial support to farmers.
 
• Under this scheme, eligible farmers receive ₹6000 per year.
 
• The amount is distributed in three equal installments of ₹2000 each.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to ensure a life of dignity for small and marginal farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• PM-KISAN

 
 
• The scheme was launched in February 2019 by the Government of India.
 
• It is aimed at providing income support to small and marginal farmers.
 
• The financial benefit is transferred directly to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries.
 
• Farmers holding up to 2 hectares of cultivable land are eligible for this scheme.
 
 
 
• Other Agricultural Schemes
 
 
• Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
 
 
• Launched in 2016, it aims to provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure.
 
• It covers risks such as natural calamities, pests, and diseases.
 
 
 
• Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)
 
 
• Launched in 2015, it aims to enhance the physical access of water on farms and expand the cultivable area under assured irrigation.
 
• It focuses on water-use efficiency and water conservation practices.
 
 
 
• Soil Health Card Scheme
 
 
• Launched in 2015, this scheme aims to promote soil testing and provide soil health cards to farmers.
 
• It helps farmers to understand the nutrient status of their soil and take corrective measures.

questions.question: Which state's government introduced the Gyan Sahayak Scheme in July, aiming at addressing teacher vacancies in government schools through contractual appointments?

• The state government of Gujarat introduced the Gyan Sahayak Scheme in July 2023, aimed at addressing teacher vacancies in government schools through contractual appointments.
 
• However, the scheme has faced significant opposition from various quarters, including student groups, political parties, and teachers’ associations.

questions.question: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed between Congress and Muslim League?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1916**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The Lucknow Pact 

 
• The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an understanding between the Congress and Muslim League.
 
• Congress accepted electorates.
 
• The Lucknow Pact was an agreement reached between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League (AIML) at a joint session of both the parties held in Lucknow in December 1916.
 
• Through the pact, the two parties agreed to allow representation to religious minorities in the provincial legislatures.
 
• The pact was signed at the annual sessions held by both the parties to put forth the common political rules including the demands of the ‘Self Governance’ of India after the war.
 
• Mohammed Ali Jinnah, a member of both the parties had suggested in the session to put pressure on the Britishers the liberalization of the country and allow its citizens to run their own country.
 
• Due to this, there arose a friendly relationship between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League.
 
• Therefore Mohammed Ali Jinnah was given the title of, ‘Ambassador of Hindu Muslim Unity’ by the nightingale of India, Sarojini Naidu.

questions.question: To which of the following states of India does the dance form Mahasu belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahasu Dance:

 
 
• Mahasu is one of the colourful forms of the Nati folk dance of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The dance is called Mahasu presumably because it began in the region of the Mahasu Pahari-speaking area.
 
• In Himachal Pradesh, Mahasu Pahari is spoken in a veritably large region which includes further than ten lakh people.
 
• It's substantially spoken in Shimla and Solan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The chief deity of the Hanol area is Lord Mahasu.
 
• People of Hanol and nearby villages of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh worship Mahasu Devta.
 
• In the 9th century, the Mahasu Devta temple was built.
 
• Katha-Kuni or koti-banal style of architecture was used in building this temple.
 
• This ancient temple comes in the Dehradun circle of Uttarakhand.
 
• The temple is located on the bank of the Tons River or Tamas River.
 
• The sole arbiter over the mortals is believed to be Mahasu devta.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chairman of Senior Men's Selection Committee by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) in July 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajit Agarkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is the national governing body for cricket in India.
 
• The BCCI headquarters is located at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• Mumbai is known as the cricket capital of India, having produced many legendary cricketers.
 
• The BCCI was formed in December 1928 and is affiliated with the International Cricket Council (ICC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India)

 
 
• The BCCI is the wealthiest cricket board in the world, managing the Indian cricket team and organizing domestic and international cricket matches in India.
 
• It oversees cricketing activities in India and has the authority to select players, umpires, and officials to participate in international cricket events.
 
• The BCCI also organizes the Indian Premier League (IPL), one of the world's most popular and lucrative T20 cricket leagues.
 
• It is responsible for developing cricket infrastructure and promoting the sport at all levels in the country.
 
 
 
• Wankhede Stadium
 
 
• Wankhede Stadium, located in Mumbai, is one of the most iconic cricket stadiums in India.
 
• The stadium has hosted numerous memorable cricket matches, including the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup final, where India emerged victorious.
 
• It has a seating capacity of around 33,000 spectators and serves as the home ground for the Mumbai cricket team and the Mumbai Indians (IPL team).
 
• Named after Sheshrao Krishnarao Wankhede, a politician and the then President of the Mumbai Cricket Association, the stadium was established in 1974.
 
 
 
• International Cricket Council (ICC)
 
 
• The ICC is the global governing body for cricket, responsible for overseeing and regulating the international game.
 
• Headquartered in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, the ICC organizes major international cricket tournaments like the ICC Cricket World Cup, ICC T20 World Cup, and ICC Champions Trophy.
 
• The ICC ensures that the rules and regulations of cricket are uniformly followed by its member countries.
 
• It also appoints match officials for international matches and works towards the development and promotion of cricket worldwide.
